item.title: Does AI imitate human conversations?
item.description:
Reflection on Presentation:

The presentation of group 3 which is on the turing test and asking the question “Can machines think? ” caught my attention the most and I found it more interesting. In this world which is fully filled with AI, AI plays an important role in our everyday life. I started thinking more deeply about the way how the AI actually works.

The group explained the complex topic in a simple and easier way to understand which I liked most from that group presentation. I understand the main idea behind the turing test which is interesting by the group’s explanation using the imitation game. The concept of it, which is focused on whether machines can imitate human conversations or it is truly like humans. I got to know about the development of AI over the time through the examples they used like the comparison between ELIZA and GPT-4.

item.title: Practical learning is fair than theoretical
item.description:
In unit 4, we spent a lot of time and looked around on the tools Metabase and Chatbot, which made this unit more engaging and practical. While exploring both of these two tools, it’s kind of exciting and also challenging as I don’t have any experience in working with these kinds of tools.

In the beginning, as I don’t have any experience with these tools I feel more challenging. There is also a need for patience, to learn how to organise data properly, creating chatbot’s responses and making dashboards and graphs.  The inaccurate responses from chatbot, confusion and getting clarity in making charts are movements which made me more struggling. But from these things, I found that in the learning process making mistakes is also a part of it.

item.title: Learnings from system failures and human errors
item.description:
Learning about failure sounds very controversial and has different perspectives among everyone. In contrast to studying successful technologies which are familiar, in this unit we deeply think about the failure, how it happened and why it happened which is not usual.

From this unit, I learnt that failures are not happening because of the single mistake. Some of the small errors in designing, software or decisions made by humans are also the reasons behind the failures. In Information systems, careful planning and testing are the most important things. Sometimes mistakes can also be made by widely known organizations as well.

item.title: Kind of Challenging Yet Valuable Learning
item.description: In the nature of information problems, it sounds both familiar and challenging at the same time while learning. As I did Math and Computer science in my higher secondary education, the concepts like binary numbers and conversations are somehow familiar to me. It helped me to feel a kind of ease in the beginning. But when these simple concepts get distributed within the concepts like image transformation and optimization problems, it becomes more complicated and needs deeper understanding.

item.title: Seeing Information in a New Way
item.description: Learning some different things in an unusual way is kind of interesting and spectacular for me, which gets my attention even though I’m not having it. I get to know about the basic difference between the data, information, knowledge and wisdom through the DIKW model in a better way. Before I went through these terms in this unit, I thought these words are almost similar. But now the difference between them and how it depends on context, meaning, and insights was quite new to me.
